input.summary:
Complete source ledger built and closed with no untraced item. Authority used: input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (which is a truncated duplicate of the disclosure and adds nothing); input/brief.md used only for formalities (no priority claim -> "Not applicable"; no federal sponsorship -> "Not applicable"; apparatus + method claims present; no "means" language anywhere; all preserved terms - rail, fixed fence, guide carriage, drill bushing, clamp knob, clamping shoe, spacer plate, pointer, center index, sight notch - appear in the text).

CLAIMS: all 22 claims traced limitation by limitation. Claim 1 (rail, flat lower face, upper face, first/second ends, first/second longitudinal sides, through slot, distance marks alongside the slot; fence releasably secured at the first end by two screws in two corresponding mounting holes, perpendicular, downwardly projecting portion, first/second orientations by removal-inversion-reinstallation, marked face outward in both) traces to "A fixed fence is attached at the first end...", "It is secured to the first end of the rail by two screws received in two corresponding holes", and "Removing the screws, turning the fence over, and reinstalling the screws moves the downwardly projecting part... from one longitudinal side... to the opposite... This lets the same marked upper face be used...". Carriage limitations (separate carriages seated on the upper face, key into slot preventing rotation while permitting sliding, cylindrical drill bushing whose bore passes completely through and registers with the slot, clamp knob above the rail with threaded shank through carriage and slot into a clamping shoe below the rail, clamping between carriage and shoe, parallel bores perpendicular to the flat lower face, first and second pointers aligned with their bore axes and readable against the distance marks) trace verbatim to the corresponding disclosure paragraphs. Claims 2, 3, 8, 12 trace to "Two separate guide carriages", "The difference between the two pointer readings is therefore the center-to-center hole spacing", "the same marked upper face", and "clamps the rail between the carriage and the shoe / Loosening the knob allows the carriage to slide". Claims 4-6 trace to "transverse center index at its midpoint" and "shallow V-shaped sight notch is formed in the second end... aligned with the center index"; spacing-apart is the direct consequence of midpoint vs second end and alignment with a "pencil centerline" is disclosed. Claims 7, 15, 19 trace to the spacer-plate paragraph ("parallel opposite faces and changes the setback of every guided hole by its thickness without changing the separation"). Claims 9, 17 trace to "The drill bushings are replaceable wear parts and are made from hardened metal"; claim 10 to the polymer/metal materials sentence (bushings correctly excluded); claims 11, 22 to "The tool has no motor, battery, electronic sensor, or network connection" plus "reusable hand tool" and "No part remains attached to the workpiece". Claims 13-16 duplicate supported matter, with "fixed fence... not slidable along the rail" traced to "A fixed fence is attached at the first end of the rail". Method claims 18-21 follow the disclosure's own use paragraph step for step (select spacing, loosen both knobs, slide to readings differing by the desired spacing and centered about the center index, tighten, place lower face, press fence or installed spacer plate to the edge, align sight notch and center index with the pencil centerline, drill both bushings, lift away with nothing left attached) and the fence-reversal paragraph.

NUMERALS: all 27 entries (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 24, 26, 30, 32, 34, 36, 40, 50, 52, 54, 58, 60, 62, 70, 72, 74, 78, 80, 82, 90, 92, 94) each denote one part only, each appears in the detailed description, and each appears in at least one figure brief; no numeral is used in the text that is absent from the ledger, and each figure's "Numerals shown" list exactly matches the numerals verbalized in that brief.

FIGURES: FIG. 1-7 briefs assert only disclosed structures. Cross-checked parentheticals (14/FIG. 4, 12/FIG. 3, 16 and 18/FIG. 2, 52-54-58-60/FIG. 5, 72-74-78-80/FIG. 3, 62 and 82/FIG. 2, 24-26-94/FIG. 7, 40/FIG. 4, 34-36/FIG. 6) all resolve to briefs that carry those numerals. Section lines verified: FIG. 2 places the same designation 3 at both endpoints of the line crossing the second guide carriage 70 and the same designation 5 at both endpoints of the line crossing the first guide carriage 50, with arrows given for each, matching the FIG. 3 and FIG. 5 brief titles, the Brief Description, and the detailed description's statement that 3-3 passes through carriage 70 and 5-5 through carriage 50. Functional-surface geometry checked specifically: the sight notch is described only as "shallow V-shaped... formed in the second end... aligned with the transverse center index", which is the inventor's own wording, with no depth, included angle, taper, runout, vertex offset, or contact statement added; the longitudinal slot, key, clamping shoe, mounting-hole joint, and spacer-plate faces likewise carry no undisclosed depth, angle, proportion, or contact topology. The unnamed "plain round body" on each carriage in FIG. 1 is expressly "shown schematically", corresponds to the disclosed clamp knob above each carriage, adds no function or relationship, and is not verbalized anywhere in the application text; it therefore stands as a permitted depiction convention. No "by way of example", "any closed outline", or similar renderer-justifying language appears in the specification, and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative, or internal comment remains. Background prior-art characterizations were left for the later prior-art trace, as instructed. Abstract is a single paragraph of 149 words with no means language. Every relationship and term used in the claims (registers with the slot, depending key, clamping between carriage and shoe, pointer aligned with bore axis, centered about the transverse center index) is used identically in the description and figure briefs.

content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all seven figure briefs, and built a limitation-by-limitation ledger against the disclosure.

input.summary: Full source-fidelity preflight completed. I traced every limitation of all 22 claims (apparatus claims 1-12, apparatus claims 13-17, method claims 18-22), every entry in draft/numerals.md (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 24, 26, 30, 32, 34, 36, 40, 50, 52, 54, 58, 60, 62, 70, 72, 74, 78, 80, 82, 90, 92, 94), every numbered part and structural/functional/material/positional statement in the Summary, Detailed Description and Abstract, and all seven figure briefs (FIG. 1-FIG. 7) back to affirmative passages in input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (which duplicates the disclosure and is truncated mid-sentence at "The difference between", adding nothing beyond the disclosure). The core ledger traces cleanly: rail with flat lower face, upper face, straight longitudinal slot and printed distance marks beside the slot; fixed fence at the first end, perpendicular to the rail, with a downwardly projecting portion bearing on the workpiece edge; two-screw/two-hole reversible mounting that moves the projecting portion from one longitudinal side to the opposite side while the same marked upper face is used; removable spacer plate with parallel opposite faces changing setback by its thickness without changing hole separation; two separate guide carriages seated on the upper face, each with a lower key in the slot that blocks rotation while allowing sliding, one cylindrical drill bushing whose bore passes completely through the carriage and registers with the slot, parallel bores perpendicular to the flat lower face, a threaded clamp knob whose shank passes through the carriage and slot into a clamping shoe below the rail, and its own pointer aligned with its bore axis and read against the distance marks with the difference of readings being the center-to-center spacing; transverse center index at the rail midpoint; shallow V-shaped sight notch in the second end aligned with the index; the disclosed method sequence; rigid polymer or metal parts with hardened-metal replaceable bushings; and the express absence of motor, battery, electronic sensor and network connection. Numeral integrity checks pass: no numeral is used for two different parts, no numeral appears in the text that is absent from the ledger, and every ledger numeral appears in at least one figure brief. Section-line designations are consistent in all three places (FIG. 2 brief places line 3-3 across the second guide carriage 70 with matching "3" at both endpoints and line 5-5 across the first guide carriage 50 with matching "5" at both endpoints; draft/07-drawings.md and draft/08-detailed-description.md recite the same designations and the same sectioned carriages). No drafting note, placeholder, open question, bracketed alternative or internal comment remains; the "shown schematically" convention stays confined to the figure briefs and is never verbalized as "by way of example" or "any closed outline" in the application text; the abstract is 146 words. Three defects were found and are reported: (1) an untraced functional allocation in the Detailed Description asserting that the sight notch and center index sighting "fix the position of the jig ... in the direction along the workpiece edge 92", where the inventor instead assigns the position of the pair relative to the centerline to the two pointer readings; (2) FIG. 1 depicts two unidentified "plain round body" elements carrying no numeral and no identification; and (3) FIG. 4 is captioned a side elevation of the drilling jig but its brief omits the guide carriages entirely. Each finding includes the candidate wording, the nearest source passage showing the gap, and a filing-clean automatic fix.

findings.title: Untraced functional allocation: sight notch and center index said to fix jig position "in the direction along the workpiece edge"
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "Referring to FIG. 7" (last sentence) and the following "The jig makes three settings" paragraph (third sentence)
findings.detail: The description invents a third, separately allocated setting function and states the direction it controls. The inventor never states that the sight notch and the transverse center index fix the jig's position in the along-edge direction, and never divides control into three settings. The disclosure allocates control in two statements only: the fence controls setback, and the two pointer readings control hole separation and the position of the pair relative to the centerline; the notch and index are described only as features the user aligns with a pencil centerline. The directional/functional attribution ("in the direction along the workpiece edge 92") and the re-attribution of pointer control to "the position of the pair along the rail 10" are drafter-supplied geometry, not inventor matter. There is no affirmative passage in input/disclosure.md or the USER passage in input/conversation.md assigning any positional control to the notch or index, nor any passage naming the along-edge direction.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "the sight notch 26 and the transverse center index 24 are spaced apart along the rail 10 so that the two sightings together fix the position of the jig on the workpiece 90 in the direction along the workpiece edge 92." Candidate: "The transverse center index 24 and the sight notch 26, sighted together on the centerline 94, set the position of the pair on the workpiece 90 in the direction along the workpiece edge 92." Nearest source (shows the gap): "The user can align the center index and the sight notch with a pencil centerline on the workpiece before tightening both carriage knobs. The fence controls setback from the workpiece edge, while the two pointer readings control hole separation and the position of the pair relative to the centerline." The disclosure contains no statement about an along-edge direction or about the notch/index controlling position.
findings.fix: In the FIG. 7 paragraph, replace "and the sight notch 26 and the transverse center index 24 are spaced apart along the rail 10 so that the two sightings together fix the position of the jig on the workpiece 90 in the direction along the workpiece edge 92." with "and the sight notch 26 and the transverse center index 24 are spaced apart along the rail 10." In the "three settings" paragraph, replace the opening "The jig makes three settings, as follows." with "The settings of the jig are made as follows.", replace "The readings of the first pointer 62 and the second pointer 82 against the distance marks 18 set the separation between the two holes and the position of the pair along the rail 10." with "The readings of the first pointer 62 and the second pointer 82 against the distance marks 18 set the separation between the two holes and the position of the pair relative to the centerline 94.", and replace "The transverse center index 24 and the sight notch 26, sighted together on the centerline 94, set the position of the pair on the workpiece 90 in the direction along the workpiece edge 92." with "The transverse center index 24 and the sight notch 26 are aligned with the centerline 94." No claim amendment is required; claim 6 recites only that the notch and index are spaced apart and alignable together with the centerline, both of which are traceable.

findings.title: FIG. 1 depicts two unidentified, unnumbered "plain round body" elements
findings.where: figures/FIG-1.md, second paragraph, and the "Numerals shown on this figure" list of figures/FIG-1.md
findings.detail: The FIG. 1 brief instructs that an anonymous round body be drawn on top of each guide carriage, but assigns it no name and no reference numeral, so the rendered view will contain two structures that the application never identifies. The disclosed part occupying that position is the threaded clamp knob above the rail (numerals 58 and 78 in the ledger), which the Detailed Description references only to FIG. 5 and FIG. 3. As written the elements are ambiguous on their face (they could equally read as the drill bushings 54 and 74, which are also carried above the carriage bodies). The added comparative statement "of like size" is a relational assertion the inventor did not make and should not be verbalized in the brief.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "A plain round body stands on top of the first guide carriage 50 and a plain round body of like size stands on top of the second guide carriage 70, both shown schematically." Source support for the part itself: "Each carriage has a threaded clamp knob above the rail." Ledger: "58 | clamp knob of the first guide carriage" and "78 | clamp knob of the second guide carriage". The FIG. 1 numeral list contains neither 58 nor 78.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-1.md replace "A plain round body stands on top of the first guide carriage 50 and a plain round body of like size stands on top of the second guide carriage 70, both shown schematically." with "A clamp knob 58 stands above the first guide carriage 50 and a clamp knob 78 stands above the second guide carriage 70, each shown schematically as a plain round body." Add to the FIG. 1 numeral list: "- 58: clamp knob of the first guide carriage" and "- 78: clamp knob of the second guide carriage". No change to the application text is needed, since the Detailed Description already recites clamp knob 58 and clamp knob 78 above the rail.

findings.title: FIG. 4 is captioned a side elevation of the drilling jig but its brief omits the guide carriages
findings.where: draft/07-drawings.md, FIG. 4 entry; figures/FIG-4.md (whole brief and numeral list)
findings.detail: The Brief Description designates FIG. 4 as a side elevation view of the drilling jig on a workpiece, but the figure brief specifies only the rail 10, lower face 14, fence 30, projecting portion 32, spacer plate 40, workpiece 90 and workpiece edge 92. The first guide carriage 50 and second guide carriage 70, which the disclosure places on the upper face of the rail and which would be visible in a side elevation of the assembled jig, are absent, so the caption and the depicted content disagree and the view would show an incomplete jig.
findings.evidence: draft/07-drawings.md: "FIG. 4 is a side elevation view of the drilling jig on a workpiece with a spacer plate installed." figures/FIG-4.md numeral list: "- 10: rail / - 14: lower face / - 30: fence / - 32: downwardly projecting portion / - 40: spacer plate / - 90: workpiece / - 92: workpiece edge" (no 50 or 70). Source for the omitted structure: "Two separate guide carriages sit on the upper face of the rail."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-4.md add, after the sentence "The rail 10 rests on the workpiece 90, with its lower face 14 on the workpiece.", the sentence "A first guide carriage 50 and a second guide carriage 70 are seated on the upper face of the rail 10, the first guide carriage 50 nearer the fence 30.", and add to the FIG. 4 numeral list "- 50: first guide carriage" and "- 70: second guide carriage". No new structure or relationship is introduced, and no change to the application text is required.

structured_output.summary: Full source-fidelity preflight completed. I traced every limitation of all 22 claims (apparatus claims 1-12, apparatus claims 13-17, method claims 18-22), every entry in draft/numerals.md (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 24, 26, 30, 32, 34, 36, 40, 50, 52, 54, 58, 60, 62, 70, 72, 74, 78, 80, 82, 90, 92, 94), every numbered part and structural/functional/material/positional statement in the Summary, Detailed Description and Abstract, and all seven figure briefs (FIG. 1-FIG. 7) back to affirmative passages in input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (which duplicates the disclosure and is truncated mid-sentence at "The difference between", adding nothing beyond the disclosure). The core ledger traces cleanly: rail with flat lower face, upper face, straight longitudinal slot and printed distance marks beside the slot; fixed fence at the first end, perpendicular to the rail, with a downwardly projecting portion bearing on the workpiece edge; two-screw/two-hole reversible mounting that moves the projecting portion from one longitudinal side to the opposite side while the same marked upper face is used; removable spacer plate with parallel opposite faces changing setback by its thickness without changing hole separation; two separate guide carriages seated on the upper face, each with a lower key in the slot that blocks rotation while allowing sliding, one cylindrical drill bushing whose bore passes completely through the carriage and registers with the slot, parallel bores perpendicular to the flat lower face, a threaded clamp knob whose shank passes through the carriage and slot into a clamping shoe below the rail, and its own pointer aligned with its bore axis and read against the distance marks with the difference of readings being the center-to-center spacing; transverse center index at the rail midpoint; shallow V-shaped sight notch in the second end aligned with the index; the disclosed method sequence; rigid polymer or metal parts with hardened-metal replaceable bushings; and the express absence of motor, battery, electronic sensor and network connection. Numeral integrity checks pass: no numeral is used for two different parts, no numeral appears in the text that is absent from the ledger, and every ledger numeral appears in at least one figure brief. Section-line designations are consistent in all three places (FIG. 2 brief places line 3-3 across the second guide carriage 70 with matching "3" at both endpoints and line 5-5 across the first guide carriage 50 with matching "5" at both endpoints; draft/07-drawings.md and draft/08-detailed-description.md recite the same designations and the same sectioned carriages). No drafting note, placeholder, open question, bracketed alternative or internal comment remains; the "shown schematically" convention stays confined to the figure briefs and is never verbalized as "by way of example" or "any closed outline" in the application text; the abstract is 146 words. Three defects were found and are reported: (1) an untraced functional allocation in the Detailed Description asserting that the sight notch and center index sighting "fix the position of the jig ... in the direction along the workpiece edge 92", where the inventor instead assigns the position of the pair relative to the centerline to the two pointer readings; (2) FIG. 1 depicts two unidentified "plain round body" elements carrying no numeral and no identification; and (3) FIG. 4 is captioned a side elevation of the drilling jig but its brief omits the guide carriages entirely. Each finding includes the candidate wording, the nearest source passage showing the gap, and a filing-clean automatic fix.

findings.title: Untraced functional allocation: sight notch and center index said to fix jig position "in the direction along the workpiece edge"
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "Referring to FIG. 7" (last sentence) and the following "The jig makes three settings" paragraph (third sentence)
findings.detail: The description invents a third, separately allocated setting function and states the direction it controls. The inventor never states that the sight notch and the transverse center index fix the jig's position in the along-edge direction, and never divides control into three settings. The disclosure allocates control in two statements only: the fence controls setback, and the two pointer readings control hole separation and the position of the pair relative to the centerline; the notch and index are described only as features the user aligns with a pencil centerline. The directional/functional attribution ("in the direction along the workpiece edge 92") and the re-attribution of pointer control to "the position of the pair along the rail 10" are drafter-supplied geometry, not inventor matter. There is no affirmative passage in input/disclosure.md or the USER passage in input/conversation.md assigning any positional control to the notch or index, nor any passage naming the along-edge direction.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "the sight notch 26 and the transverse center index 24 are spaced apart along the rail 10 so that the two sightings together fix the position of the jig on the workpiece 90 in the direction along the workpiece edge 92." Candidate: "The transverse center index 24 and the sight notch 26, sighted together on the centerline 94, set the position of the pair on the workpiece 90 in the direction along the workpiece edge 92." Nearest source (shows the gap): "The user can align the center index and the sight notch with a pencil centerline on the workpiece before tightening both carriage knobs. The fence controls setback from the workpiece edge, while the two pointer readings control hole separation and the position of the pair relative to the centerline." The disclosure contains no statement about an along-edge direction or about the notch/index controlling position.
findings.fix: In the FIG. 7 paragraph, replace "and the sight notch 26 and the transverse center index 24 are spaced apart along the rail 10 so that the two sightings together fix the position of the jig on the workpiece 90 in the direction along the workpiece edge 92." with "and the sight notch 26 and the transverse center index 24 are spaced apart along the rail 10." In the "three settings" paragraph, replace the opening "The jig makes three settings, as follows." with "The settings of the jig are made as follows.", replace "The readings of the first pointer 62 and the second pointer 82 against the distance marks 18 set the separation between the two holes and the position of the pair along the rail 10." with "The readings of the first pointer 62 and the second pointer 82 against the distance marks 18 set the separation between the two holes and the position of the pair relative to the centerline 94.", and replace "The transverse center index 24 and the sight notch 26, sighted together on the centerline 94, set the position of the pair on the workpiece 90 in the direction along the workpiece edge 92." with "The transverse center index 24 and the sight notch 26 are aligned with the centerline 94." No claim amendment is required; claim 6 recites only that the notch and index are spaced apart and alignable together with the centerline, both of which are traceable.

findings.title: FIG. 1 depicts two unidentified, unnumbered "plain round body" elements
findings.where: figures/FIG-1.md, second paragraph, and the "Numerals shown on this figure" list of figures/FIG-1.md
findings.detail: The FIG. 1 brief instructs that an anonymous round body be drawn on top of each guide carriage, but assigns it no name and no reference numeral, so the rendered view will contain two structures that the application never identifies. The disclosed part occupying that position is the threaded clamp knob above the rail (numerals 58 and 78 in the ledger), which the Detailed Description references only to FIG. 5 and FIG. 3. As written the elements are ambiguous on their face (they could equally read as the drill bushings 54 and 74, which are also carried above the carriage bodies). The added comparative statement "of like size" is a relational assertion the inventor did not make and should not be verbalized in the brief.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "A plain round body stands on top of the first guide carriage 50 and a plain round body of like size stands on top of the second guide carriage 70, both shown schematically." Source support for the part itself: "Each carriage has a threaded clamp knob above the rail." Ledger: "58 | clamp knob of the first guide carriage" and "78 | clamp knob of the second guide carriage". The FIG. 1 numeral list contains neither 58 nor 78.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-1.md replace "A plain round body stands on top of the first guide carriage 50 and a plain round body of like size stands on top of the second guide carriage 70, both shown schematically." with "A clamp knob 58 stands above the first guide carriage 50 and a clamp knob 78 stands above the second guide carriage 70, each shown schematically as a plain round body." Add to the FIG. 1 numeral list: "- 58: clamp knob of the first guide carriage" and "- 78: clamp knob of the second guide carriage". No change to the application text is needed, since the Detailed Description already recites clamp knob 58 and clamp knob 78 above the rail.

findings.title: FIG. 4 is captioned a side elevation of the drilling jig but its brief omits the guide carriages
findings.where: draft/07-drawings.md, FIG. 4 entry; figures/FIG-4.md (whole brief and numeral list)
findings.detail: The Brief Description designates FIG. 4 as a side elevation view of the drilling jig on a workpiece, but the figure brief specifies only the rail 10, lower face 14, fence 30, projecting portion 32, spacer plate 40, workpiece 90 and workpiece edge 92. The first guide carriage 50 and second guide carriage 70, which the disclosure places on the upper face of the rail and which would be visible in a side elevation of the assembled jig, are absent, so the caption and the depicted content disagree and the view would show an incomplete jig.
findings.evidence: draft/07-drawings.md: "FIG. 4 is a side elevation view of the drilling jig on a workpiece with a spacer plate installed." figures/FIG-4.md numeral list: "- 10: rail / - 14: lower face / - 30: fence / - 32: downwardly projecting portion / - 40: spacer plate / - 90: workpiece / - 92: workpiece edge" (no 50 or 70). Source for the omitted structure: "Two separate guide carriages sit on the upper face of the rail."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-4.md add, after the sentence "The rail 10 rests on the workpiece 90, with its lower face 14 on the workpiece.", the sentence "A first guide carriage 50 and a second guide carriage 70 are seated on the upper face of the rail 10, the first guide carriage 50 nearer the fence 30.", and add to the FIG. 4 numeral list "- 50: first guide carriage" and "- 70: second guide carriage". No new structure or relationship is introduced, and no change to the application text is required.
